description: Replace the random SLSQP start with a Lubachevsky-style inflation start: random centres grow their radii toward the largest feasible values, overlapping centres are pushed apart, and SLSQP then polishes the jammed result.

Replace the random SLSQP start with a mirror-symmetric start: half the centres are drawn in the left half of the square and mirrored to the right, an odd n gets one centre on the midline, and a coin flip swaps x and y to choose vertical or horizontal symmetry.

Adds a rattler relocation pass after the random restarts: circles with fewer than two near-contacts (gap below 1e-4) in the best packing are moved to random centres, SLSQP re-optimises from that start, and the result is kept only if the repaired radius sum improves.

Turns the random-restart loop into basin hopping: each step perturbs the current packing's centres and re-optimises with SLSQP, accepts worse packings with probability exp((new-old)/T) under a geometric T schedule from 0.01 to 1e-4, and tracks the best packing separately.

Adds a remove-and-reinsert move that, half the time, takes the best packing, moves its smallest circle to the largest-clearance point among 2000 random samples, and re-runs SLSQP from there, with the existing acceptance rule deciding what is kept.

Replace the annealed basin hopping in solve with the spec's greedy version: perturb the best packing (centre noise 0.03, radii scaled by U[0.8,1.0]), re-optimise, keep only strict improvements, and restart from a fresh random layout one time in five.
Initialise the radii of each fresh SLSQP start from uniform draws in [0.02, 0.12] instead of the constant 0.05, so that restarts begin from different size distributions.

issues: Integrity: I found nothing wrong. There is no file or network access, no pasted coordinates and no use of labels. The added randomness-free LP polish only refines the packing that the existing search already found.

Validity: every LP step ends with the existing _repair on clipped centres. The radius lower bound max(-tr, -r) keeps radii non-negative. So the final packing goes through the same validity path as the incumbent, and I found no bug that would make the result meaningless.

Timing risk (not a veto): _lp_polish runs after the main loop has already used 80% of the 30 s budget, and nothing checks time_limit inside it. It can run up to 100 HiGHS solves, each on a dense matrix of about 624x96 rebuilt every iteration, which should take a few seconds. That likely stays under 30 s and almost surely under the 45 s void limit, but adding a time check inside the polish loop would be safer.

Plausibility: the candidate's mean of 2.9372 is slightly above the 'about 2.9370' best published value. The harness checks validity exactly, so this probably reflects the rounding in 'about'. Still, it is worth confirming with a replicate.

Statistics: the difference is 0.0017, from one run each. With sd 0.0034 per job, z = 0.0017/(0.0034*sqrt(2)) ≈ 0.35. The harness's 0.337 is consistent with that once the 4-decimal rounding of the inputs is taken into account. The evidence is weak and the provisional reject is correct for now. The idea is reasonable, so a replicate may be worth a slot.

description: Adds a final sequential-LP polish that linearises all pair and wall constraints at the best packing, solves a highs linprog maximising the radius sum inside a 1e-3 trust region, keeps a step only if the repaired packing has a larger radius sum, and shrinks the trust region otherwise.
Radii-first two-stage start: random centres with zero radii, a containment-plus-overlap-penalty radius maximisation, then full SLSQP, as a new starting scheme.

Replace the single basin-hopping chain with an elite pool of 8 packings, where each step after the pool fills runs SLSQP from a child that takes circles left of a random cut from one parent and the rest from another, replacing the worst member if the child scores higher.

Sparse neighbour-pair constraints: SLSQP includes only pairs whose centres are within 2*max radius + 0.15 at the start, then recomputes all pair distances after each solve and adds any excluded overlapping pairs and re-solves, for at most 3 rounds.

Sparse neighbour-pair constraints: SLSQP includes only pairs whose centres are within 2*max radius + 0.15 at the start, then recomputes all pair distances after each solve and adds any excluded overlapping pairs and re-solves, for at most 3 rounds.
Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.93 so each solve call uses about 27.9 s of the 30 s CPU budget, keeping the existing time.process_time check.
Over-pack n+1 circles with one SLSQP solve and repair, drop the smallest-radius circle, and start the existing basin-hopping loop from that n-circle packing.

Before the SLSQP solve of each fresh random start, run five L-BFGS-B stages (penalty weight 10 to 1e5) on minus the radius sum plus weighted squared overlap and wall violations, with an analytic gradient, and use the result as the SLSQP start.

issues: No integrity problem: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, randomness still comes from rng, and the SLSQP and repair steps still run, so the exact validity check still applies.
I checked the gradient of the soft-min penalty by hand for pairs, walls and radii, and it is correct. The penalty switches off when L <= 0, so the gradient has a jump there; this is harmless.

Design weakness: _soft_stage runs on every _solve_once call, including when x0 is passed in, so it may disturb refinement of a good solution. Its cost (6 x 300 L-BFGS-B iterations over 496 pairs) also leaves fewer restarts in the time budget, which probably explains the lower score.
Recomputed z = -(0.0085)/(0.0034*sqrt(2)) = -1.77. It matches the harness's -1.757 within rounding. The candidate is worse by about 1.8 sd, so rejecting is consistent.

description: Before each hard-constraint SLSQP solve, run a log-sum-exp soft-min penalty continuation (mu from 10 to 1e4 over 6 L-BFGS-B stages, analytic gradient) over centres and radii, then pass the result to SLSQP.
Raise the SLSQP iteration cap from 200 to 1000 and set ftol to 1e-12 so each restart runs closer to convergence, with the outer time check unchanged.

Basin hopping restarts from a fresh random SLSQP packing after 25 consecutive steps without a new global best, and the temperature clock is reset to each chain's own start time, so each chain cools over its own elapsed time.

Pass an analytic Jacobian of the SLSQP constraints (pair distances, walls, radii) and a constant objective gradient to minimize, replacing the finite-difference Jacobian so each SLSQP iteration is much cheaper.

Seed the first fresh SLSQP start with a hexagonal-lattice patch (thinned or padded to 32 centres, small uniform radii) half the time, but aborted because the incumbent only makes one fresh start per solve call.

Give each SLSQP restart random per-circle objective weights uniform(0.8, 1.2) drawn from rng, so the local searches climb to different optima, while constraints and the unweighted scoring of returned packings stay unchanged.

Basin-hopping steps now alternate at random: half replace all circles within a random radius R in [0.2, 0.4] of a random point with fresh uniform centres and radius INIT_RADIUS, and half keep the existing small global Gaussian kick.

Adds a stagnation-triggered reheat: after 30 basin-hopping steps without a new best radius sum, cur is reset to best and the temperature schedule restarts at T=0.003 and decays to 1e-4 over the remaining budget.

issues: No integrity problems. The diff does not read or write files, contains no hard-coded coordinates, and uses no labels. Its only randomness is the permutation order, which comes from the seeded rng.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. _grow only raises radius i to min(distance to the nearest wall, min over j of d_ij - r_j), with the circle's own distance set to inf. This keeps the packing valid up to about 1e-16 of rounding, which is far below the 1e-10 tolerance. If _repair leaves a radius at or above its limit, that radius is left unchanged. Updating radii one at a time in place is correct.

Recomputed z: the candidate loss is -2.9338 and the incumbent loss is -2.9355. Lower is better, so the candidate is worse by 0.0017. With one run on each side, the standard error is 0.0034*sqrt(2) ≈ 0.00481, which gives z ≈ -0.353. The harness reports -0.360, and the gap fits the inputs being rounded to 4 decimals.

Only one run on each side, so the comparison has little power. A difference of 0.0017 is about half the noise sd of one job. Rejecting is reasonable, but the evidence does not show that the edit causes harm.
Side effect: annealing now compares the grown radii, and the grown radii are carried into the next warm start. This is intended behaviour, not a bug.

description: Adds a greedy sequential radius-growth pass after _repair (two random-order sweeps, each circle grown to the largest radius its walls and neighbours allow), run on every candidate before the acceptance test.

Basin-hopping steps now move only one or two randomly chosen circles (uniform relocation with probability 0.5, otherwise a 0.05-scale jitter), set their radius to half the packing's minimum radius, and keep all other circles in place for the warm start.

Replace the single annealed basin-hopping chain with 4 fixed-temperature chains on a geometric ladder from 1e-4 to 1e-2, advanced round-robin, with Metropolis swaps of adjacent rungs every 10 rounds and a global best tracked across all chains.

Adds a global compression/expansion hop to basin hopping: with probability 0.3 all centres are scaled about (0.5, 0.5) by a factor uniform in [0.9, 1.1], clipped to the square and repaired to fit before the SLSQP solve, otherwise the existing per-circle Gaussian perturbation is used; acceptance is unchanged.
Rescale the SLSQP radius variables by 10 inside _solve_once so centres and radii have comparable magnitude, then unscale the radii before returning them to the existing repair step.

Adds a cluster rotation move to basin hopping: with probability 0.3, the centres within 0.25 of a random point are rotated about their centroid by uniform(-0.3, 0.3) radians before the usual SLSQP warm start, and otherwise the existing Gaussian per-circle perturbation is used.

Before the n-circle basin hopping, run basin hopping on n-1 circles for 25% of the budget, insert one circle at the grid point of largest clearance with radius 0.01, warm-start SLSQP on all n circles from that, then continue basin hopping on n circles for the rest of the budget.

Adds a gravity-shear hop to basin hopping: half the steps shift every centre by one common random displacement of length 0.02 to 0.1 in a random direction, plus N(0, 0.01) jitter, and scale the radii by 0.9 before the usual SLSQP solve and repair.

Fresh SLSQP starts place the n centres one per cell of the smallest m x m grid (m = ceil(sqrt(n))) chosen by a random permutation, jittered by plus or minus 0.4 cell width and clipped to [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW], with radii at INIT_RADIUS; hop steps and the SLSQP call are unchanged.

Fresh SLSQP starts place the n centres one per cell of the smallest m x m grid (m = ceil(sqrt(n))) chosen by a random permutation, jittered by plus or minus 0.4 cell width and clipped to [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW], with radii at INIT_RADIUS; hop steps and the SLSQP call are unchanged.

Replace the hand-written annealed basin hopping with scipy.optimize.basinhopping on a mu=1e3 quadratic-penalty energy, using analytic-gradient L-BFGS-B local solves and a seeded uniform step of 0.05, a time-limit callback, and a final SLSQP polish plus repair from the best penalty minimum.

With probability 0.3 in each basin-hopping step, swap the centres of a random pair of circles whose radii differ by more than 20 percent (radii stay in place), then warm-start _solve_once from that packing instead of the Gaussian perturbation.
Each basin-hopping step replaces the random 0.05 centre jump with 4 Lloyd iterations on a 60x60 grid (each adding N(0, 0.01) noise and clipping to the square) before the existing SLSQP solve.

Hard-disk Monte Carlo compression start
